props.title: In Love and War
props.initialSlug: Hemingway's WWI romance with his nurse inspires legend

sections.content: In Love and War represents one of Hollywood's attempts to dramatize Ernest Hemingway's early life, specifically focusing on his World War I experiences as an 18-year-old ambulance driver in Italy. Starring Chris O'Donnell as young Hemingway and Sandra Bullock as nurse Agnes von Kurowsky, the film captures the romance that would later inspire A Farewell to Arms (1932). Director Richard Attenborough brings his characteristic attention to period detail, though the film joins other challenging Hemingway adaptations like The Sun Also Rises (1957) and The Old Man and the Sea (1958) in struggling to translate the author's spare prose style to screen.

sections.content: The film fits into a broader category of wartime romance dramas that explore love amid conflict. The English Patient (1996) similarly uses the backdrop of war to examine passionate romance and features detailed hospital scenes. Pearl Harbor (2001) also attempts to blend historical events with a love story involving medical personnel, though with more emphasis on spectacle than In Love and War's intimate focus. SUBHEAD: Literary Adaptations and Biographical Films

As a biographical film about a major author, In Love and War shares DNA with works like Genius (2016) about Thomas Wolfe and Maxwell Perkins, and Finding Neverland (2004) about J.M. Barrie. These films attempt to dramatize the experiences that shaped great writers, though often struggle with depicting the internal creative process. The challenge of adapting Hemingway specifically has led to varied results, from the relatively successful The Killers (1946) to more uneven efforts like Islands in the Stream (1977).
